p.title: Dev's sugar test
p.challenge: Put the steps of Dev's experiment in the order of the scientific method

nodes.info: Dev notices that sugar disappears when it is stirred into water.
Does sugar dissolve faster in warm water than in cold water?
Sugar dissolves faster in warm water.
Two glasses with the same water and the same spoon of sugar. Change only one thing: warm tap water in one, cold water in the other (an adult nearby).
The sugar disappears first in the warm water.
The guess is supported: warm water dissolves sugar faster. If it had not been, Dev would make a new guess and test again.

p.title: Plant key: herb, shrub, tree, climber or creeper?
p.challenge: Meena's plant is about her height, with a hard woody stem and many branches just above the soil. Follow the key: answer each question to find its type.

nodes.info: Is it soft and green, or hard and woody? Is it strong enough to stand up on its own?

nodes.text: Is the stem too weak to stand up on its own?
Does it climb up a support?

nodes.info: Weak stem that climbs up with support, like money plant and grapevine.
Weak stem that spreads along the ground, like watermelon and pumpkin.

nodes.text: Is it short with a soft, green stem?

nodes.info: Short plant with a soft green stem, like wheat and mint.

nodes.text: Is it tall with one thick woody trunk?

nodes.info: Tall, with a thick woody trunk, like neem and mango.
Woody stem with branches starting near the ground, like rose and hibiscus.

p.title: Cleaning muddy water
p.challenge: Put the steps for cleaning muddy water in order

panels.t: Collect the muddy water in a glass.
Leave it undisturbed: heavy mud settles at the bottom (sedimentation).
Gently pour the clearer water from the top into another glass (decantation).
Pour it through filter paper: the clear filtrate passes, the residue stays (filtration).
Boil or purify the water before drinking, to kill germs we cannot see.
